name: Ahumai
overview: Ahumai was a male member of the tribe of Judah, identified specifically as the son of Jahath. His mention is brief and primarily genealogical, with no additional notes or detailed narrative provided in Scripture. This positions him within the broader lineage of Judah without further elaboration.
namesAndTitles: The name Ahumai appears once in Scripture and is presented simply as a proper name without any recorded meaning or divine origin. There is no additional information on the significance or etymology of his name.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Ahumai as the son of Jahath, establishing a direct father-son relationship. Beyond this, no other family relationships are documented for Ahumai in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Ahumai's significance lies in his inclusion within the genealogical records of the tribe of Judah, as noted in 1 Chronicles 4:2. While the text does not elaborate on his deeds or role, his mention contributes to the preservation of the tribal lineage important for understanding Israel's history and God's providential care for His people. His presence in the genealogies underscores the faithfulness of God in maintaining His covenant through successive generations.
